newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate drops on data, U.S. long bond.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate drops on data, U.S. long bond.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates closed down 150 basis points at 18.00 percent on demand triggered by low U.S. long bond yields and strong domestic economic data, dealers said.
"Jitters are over now, and fundamentals are supporting a downward trend, like inflation and unemployment. There is liquidity in the market," a dealer said.
Open unemployment fell to 3.4 percent in June from 3.9 percent in May, the National Statistics Institute (INEGI) reported during the session.
Dealers said U.S. long bond yields may have gained slightly during the session, but were still low enough to enhance confidence in the domestic markets.
"Low long bond yields suggest U.S. base rates are not about to rise," a fixed-income analyst said, referring to August's Federal Open Market Committee meeting to review U.S. interest rate policy.
U.S. 30-year Treasury bonds ended off 5/32 to yield 6.49 percent.
